en-to-be.title: The verb to be: am, is, are
en-to-be.summary: How to say “I am a student”, “she is at home”, “we are not tired”.
en-to-be.theory.0.text: Every English sentence needs a verb. Where many languages simply say “I student” or “She at home”, English uses **to be** in the right form.
en-to-be.theory.1.heading: Negatives and questions
en-to-be.theory.1.text: In a negative, **not** goes after the verb: is not = **isn’t**, are not = **aren’t**, while am not only shortens as **I’m not**. In a question the verb moves in front of the subject.
en-to-be.exercises.0.explain: My brother is he, so is.
en-to-be.exercises.2.explain: I takes only am: I am hungry (I’m hungry).
en-to-be.exercises.3.explain: In a question the verb comes first: Are they at school?
en-to-be.exercises.5.explain: You → are, negative are not / aren’t.
en-to-be.exercises.6.explain: The question starts with the verb: Is your sister…
en-to-be.exercises.8.explain: The children are they, so are.

en-present-simple.title: Present Simple: habits and facts
en-present-simple.summary: I work, she works: what happens regularly and what is always true.
en-present-simple.theory.0.text: Present Simple describes habits, things that happen regularly and general facts. Signal words: **always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day**.
en-present-simple.theory.1.heading: The -s ending with he, she, it
en-present-simple.theory.1.text: With he, she, it the verb takes **-s**: works, plays. After -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o it is **-es**: watches, goes. Consonant + y becomes **-ies**: study → studies. Have becomes **has**.
en-present-simple.theory.2.heading: Questions and negatives
en-present-simple.theory.2.text: You need the auxiliary **do**, and with he, she, it — **does**. After does the verb loses its -s.
en-present-simple.exercises.3.explain: Questions with you are made with do.
en-present-simple.exercises.4.explain: After doesn’t the verb has no -s.
en-present-simple.exercises.6.explain: With we the verb has no ending.
en-present-simple.exercises.11.explain: Late is an adjective, so you need to be: He is never late.

en-there-is.title: There is / there are: what is where
en-there-is.summary: How to say “there is a cat on the table”, “there are two museums in town”.
en-there-is.theory.0.text: To say that something **exists** or **is somewhere**, an English sentence starts with **there is** (one thing) or **there are** (several). The place usually comes at the end.
en-there-is.theory.1.heading: Negatives and questions
en-there-is.theory.1.text: Negative: **there isn’t / there aren’t**, often with **any**: there aren’t any chairs. In a question is / are moves forward: **Is there…? Are there…?** Short answers: Yes, there is. / No, there aren’t.
en-there-is.exercises.2.explain: One bank, a question: Is there…?
en-there-is.exercises.3.explain: Eggs is plural: there aren’t any eggs.
en-there-is.exercises.4.explain: The short answer repeats are: Yes, there are.
en-there-is.exercises.5.explain: One apple, a vowel sound — an apple.

en-present-continuous.title: Present Continuous: what is happening now
en-present-continuous.summary: I am reading — an action in progress, right now or these days.
en-present-continuous.theory.0.text: Present Continuous = **am / is / are + verb with -ing**. It is used for what is happening right now or around this time. Signal words: **now, at the moment, today, this week, Look!**
en-present-continuous.theory.1.heading: Spelling the -ing form
en-present-continuous.theory.1.text: A silent e drops: make → **making**. A short verb with one vowel before a final consonant doubles it: run → **running**, sit → **sitting**. ie becomes y: lie → **lying**.
en-present-continuous.theory.2.heading: Simple or Continuous?
en-present-continuous.theory.2.text: Present Simple is for regular and permanent things, Present Continuous for now. State verbs (**know, like, want, understand, believe**) are usually not used in the Continuous.
en-present-continuous.exercises.0.explain: Look! — the action is happening now: is raining.
en-present-continuous.exercises.1.explain: is + writing: the silent e drops.
en-present-continuous.exercises.3.explain: Understand is a state verb and stays in Present Simple.
en-present-continuous.exercises.4.explain: Usually means a habit, so Present Simple.
en-present-continuous.exercises.5.explain: A Continuous question starts with am / is / are: Are you listening?
en-present-continuous.exercises.9.explain: Know is a state verb: Present Simple.
en-present-continuous.exercises.10.explain: A temporary situation “this week”: is staying.

en-past-simple.title: Past Simple: what happened
en-past-simple.summary: Worked, went, saw: finished actions in the past.
en-past-simple.theory.0.text: Past Simple is for finished actions in the past. Signal words: **yesterday, last week, two years ago, in 2010**. Regular verbs take **-ed**: work → worked, live → lived, stop → **stopped**, study → **studied**.
en-past-simple.theory.1.heading: Irregular verbs
en-past-simple.theory.1.text: Some verbs change completely — they have to be learned.
en-past-simple.theory.2.heading: Questions and negatives
en-past-simple.theory.2.text: You need **did**, and the verb goes back to its base form — for regular and irregular verbs alike.
en-past-simple.exercises.3.explain: After did — the base form: buy.
en-past-simple.exercises.4.explain: A short verb: the consonant doubles — stopped.
en-past-simple.exercises.8.explain: Read is irregular: spelled the same, pronounced [red].
en-past-simple.exercises.9.explain: A past question with an ordinary verb — did.
en-past-simple.exercises.10.explain: To be in the past: was / were. We → were.

en-articles.title: Articles a, an, the
en-articles.summary: When it is “some”, when it is “that very one”, and when no article is needed.
en-articles.theory.0.text: **A / an** — one of many, mentioned for the first time. **An** goes before a vowel sound: an apple, an hour (the h is silent). But **a university** — the word starts with the sound [ju].
en-articles.theory.1.text: **The** — a specific thing, one already known or the only one of its kind.
en-articles.theory.2.heading: No article
en-articles.theory.2.text: Plurals and uncountable nouns in a general sense, names and most countries. Exceptions with the words states, kingdom, republic: **the USA, the UK**.
en-articles.exercises.0.explain: Idea starts with a vowel sound: an idea.
en-articles.exercises.1.explain: University sounds like [ju:] — a consonant sound, so a.
en-articles.exercises.2.explain: There is only one sun — the sun.
en-articles.exercises.3.explain: The book has been mentioned — now it is the book.
en-articles.exercises.5.explain: The h in hour is silent: an hour.
en-articles.exercises.8.explain: Jobs take a / an; engineer starts with a vowel sound.
en-articles.exercises.9.explain: It is clear which door — the.

en-future.title: The future: will and going to
en-future.summary: A decision on the spot, a promise or a plan already made.
en-future.theory.0.text: **Will + verb** is for decisions made while speaking, promises, offers of help and predictions with “I think…”. It shortens to **’ll**, the negative is **won’t**.
en-future.theory.1.text: **am / is / are going to + verb** is for plans and intentions thought about in advance, and for predictions based on what you can see now.
en-future.exercises.0.explain: A decision made right now — will.
en-future.exercises.1.explain: A plan made in advance — going to.
en-future.exercises.2.explain: A prediction from what you can see — going to.
en-future.exercises.4.explain: An intention: she is going to study.
en-future.exercises.5.explain: “I think…” — an opinion about the future, will.
en-future.exercises.8.explain: A conclusion from what you can see — going to.
en-future.exercises.10.explain: Going to is built with am / is / are.

en-present-perfect.title: Present Perfect: results up to now
en-present-perfect.summary: I have done: a past that matters now, and experience “ever”.
en-present-perfect.theory.0.text: Present Perfect = **have / has + past participle** (worked, seen, done). The time is not named — what matters is the result now or the experience itself.
en-present-perfect.theory.1.heading: Signal words
en-present-perfect.theory.1.text: **ever, never, already, yet, just** and a period that is not over yet: today, this week. With **for** (a length of time) and **since** (a starting point) — something that began in the past and continues: I’ve lived here **for** ten years / **since** 2015.
en-present-perfect.theory.2.heading: Perfect or Past Simple?
en-present-perfect.theory.2.text: If **when** is named (yesterday, in 2019, last week, ago), only Past Simple works. Present Perfect does not go with finished time.
en-present-perfect.exercises.0.explain: Experience with no time named: have seen.
en-present-perfect.exercises.1.explain: In 2019 is finished time: Past Simple.
en-present-perfect.exercises.2.explain: At the end of questions and negatives — yet.
en-present-perfect.exercises.3.explain: From a point in time — since.
en-present-perfect.exercises.5.explain: The result matters now: has lost.
en-present-perfect.exercises.6.explain: A question about experience: Have you ever…?
en-present-perfect.exercises.8.explain: Already goes in the middle of a statement.
en-present-perfect.exercises.9.explain: For five years and still now: have been.
en-present-perfect.exercises.10.explain: When asks about a moment in the past: Past Simple.
en-present-perfect.exercises.11.explain: Gone — she left and hasn’t come back; been — she went and came back.

en-conditionals.title: Conditionals: first and second
en-conditionals.theory.0.heading: First conditional — a real future
en-conditionals.theory.0.text: **If + Present Simple, will + verb.** The condition is quite possible. No future tense after if!
en-conditionals.theory.1.heading: Second conditional — imagined
en-conditionals.theory.1.text: **If + Past Simple, would + verb.** The situation is unlikely or unreal now. With to be, **were** is common for every person: If I were you…
en-conditionals.exercises.0.explain: After if in the first conditional — Present Simple.
en-conditionals.exercises.1.explain: A real result: will melt (for general facts melts works too).
en-conditionals.exercises.2.explain: Imagined — second conditional: if + Past Simple.
en-conditionals.exercises.5.explain: The if part can come second, but the tense is the same: Present Simple.
en-conditionals.exercises.6.explain: An unreal situation: if you were.
en-conditionals.exercises.10.explain: Unless = if not; a real future — will.

en-passive.title: The passive voice
en-passive.summary: The letter was written: when the action matters more than who did it.
en-passive.theory.0.text: Passive = **to be in the right tense + past participle**. The object of the action becomes the subject. Who did it is added with **by** if it matters.
en-passive.theory.1.heading: When to use the passive
en-passive.theory.1.text: When the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant, and in news, instructions and scientific texts.
en-passive.exercises.0.explain: The bridge was built (who built it doesn’t matter): was built.
en-passive.exercises.1.explain: A general fact, Present Simple: is grown.
en-passive.exercises.3.explain: Future passive: will be + past participle.
en-passive.exercises.6.explain: A rule with no doer: isn’t allowed.
en-passive.exercises.9.explain: The hospital will be opened — future passive.
en-passive.exercises.10.explain: Yet → Present Perfect passive: hasn’t been repaired.

en-past-perfect.title: Past Perfect and telling a story
en-past-perfect.summary: Had done: what happened before another past event.
en-past-perfect.theory.0.text: Past Perfect = **had + past participle**. It shows that one past action happened **before** another. Without it the order of events can be unclear.
en-past-perfect.theory.1.heading: Three tenses in a story
en-past-perfect.theory.1.text: Past Simple is the main chain of events, Past Continuous the background (what was going on), Past Perfect what happened even earlier. Often with **already, just, before, after, by the time**.
en-past-perfect.exercises.0.explain: The film started before I arrived: had started.
en-past-perfect.exercises.1.explain: Experience up to a past moment: hadn’t flown.
en-past-perfect.exercises.2.explain: Dinner came first: had had (had + had).
en-past-perfect.exercises.3.explain: Background, in progress when the phone rang — Past Continuous.
en-past-perfect.exercises.4.explain: By the time signals Past Perfect.
en-past-perfect.exercises.5.explain: The meeting was earlier: had met.
en-past-perfect.exercises.6.explain: A chain of actions in order — Past Simple.
en-past-perfect.exercises.9.explain: Experience up to a past moment: had been.
en-past-perfect.exercises.10.explain: Dinner was ready by the time I came: had cooked.

en-reported-speech.title: Reported speech
en-reported-speech.summary: She said she was tired: how to pass on someone’s words.
en-reported-speech.theory.0.text: When you report words after **said** or **told**, the tense usually moves one step back, and pronouns and time words change to fit.
en-reported-speech.theory.1.heading: Questions and requests
en-reported-speech.theory.1.text: A reported question uses statement word order, without do / did. A yes / no question is introduced with **if / whether**. Requests and orders — **told / asked + to + verb**.
en-reported-speech.theory.2.heading: Time and place words
en-reported-speech.theory.2.text: now → **then**, today → **that day**, tomorrow → **the next day**, yesterday → **the day before**, here → **there**. **Say** takes no person, **tell** always does: said that…, told me that…
en-reported-speech.exercises.3.explain: Statement word order and the tense shift: where I worked.
en-reported-speech.exercises.4.explain: A yes / no question — if / whether.
en-reported-speech.exercises.10.explain: A prohibition: told + not to + verb.
en-reported-speech.exercises.11.explain: A yes / no question — if / whether.

en-third-conditional.title: Third conditional and wish
en-third-conditional.summary: If I had known… — regrets about a past that can’t be changed.
en-third-conditional.theory.0.text: **If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.** It is about a past that went differently: the condition did not happen.
en-third-conditional.theory.1.heading: Mixed conditionals
en-third-conditional.theory.1.text: A past condition with a result now: **If + Past Perfect, would + verb.**
en-third-conditional.theory.2.text: Regret about the present — **wish + Past Simple**; about the past — **wish + Past Perfect**; irritation at someone’s behaviour — **wish + would**.
en-third-conditional.exercises.0.explain: Third conditional: would have + past participle.
en-third-conditional.exercises.2.explain: Mixed: a past condition, a result now — would + verb.
en-third-conditional.exercises.3.explain: Regret about the present: wish + were.
en-third-conditional.exercises.4.explain: About the past: wish + Past Perfect.
en-third-conditional.exercises.5.explain: Irritation, wanting a change — wish + would.
en-third-conditional.exercises.9.explain: Mixed: the past condition — Past Perfect.
en-third-conditional.exercises.10.explain: Regret about the past: had been.

en-inversion.title: Inversion for emphasis
en-inversion.summary: Never have I seen… — reversed word order after negative adverbs.
en-inversion.theory.0.text: When a sentence starts with a negative or limiting expression, the auxiliary verb goes **before** the subject, as in a question. It sounds more formal and more emotional.
en-inversion.theory.1.heading: Conditions without if
en-inversion.theory.1.text: In formal English if can be dropped by putting the verb first: **Had I known** = If I had known; **Should you need** help = If you need help; **Were it** not for you = If it were not for you.
en-inversion.exercises.0.explain: After Never — inversion: have I seen.
en-inversion.exercises.3.explain: Hardly … when; but No sooner … than.
en-inversion.exercises.6.explain: Only after + inversion: did I realise.

en-cleft.title: Cleft sentences
en-cleft.summary: It was Anna who… / What I need is…: how to add emphasis.
en-cleft.theory.0.text: The part you want to stress goes between **it is / it was** and **who** (for people) or **that**.
en-cleft.theory.1.text: Starting with **What** builds expectation, and the key part comes at the end after **is / was**. With an action — **What I did was (to) + verb**.
en-cleft.theory.2.heading: Other patterns
en-cleft.theory.2.text: **All I want is…**, **The thing that worries me is…**, **The reason why… is that…**, **The place where…**

en-participle-clauses.title: Participle clauses
en-participle-clauses.summary: Opening the door, she saw… — how to fold two sentences into one.
en-participle-clauses.theory.0.text: If two actions share a subject, one of them can become a participle clause. **-ing** — an active action at the same time or just before; **having + past participle** — clearly earlier; **past participle** — a passive meaning.
en-participle-clauses.theory.1.heading: Careful: one subject
en-participle-clauses.theory.1.text: The subject of the clause and of the main sentence must be the same. ✗ *Walking home, the rain started* — it sounds as if the rain was walking home. ✓ **Walking home, I got caught in the rain.**
en-participle-clauses.theory.2.heading: After a noun
en-participle-clauses.theory.2.text: The clause replaces a who / which clause: the man **sitting** next to me (= who was sitting), the books **left** on the table (= which were left).
en-participle-clauses.exercises.0.explain: An active action at the same time: Reading.
en-participle-clauses.exercises.1.explain: The tower was built — passive: Built.
en-participle-clauses.exercises.5.explain: The subject must match: I was walking to work, not the rain.
en-participle-clauses.exercises.6.explain: Not goes before the participle: Not knowing.
en-participle-clauses.exercises.8.explain: She was disturbed — passive meaning: Disturbed.
en-participle-clauses.exercises.10.explain: Earlier and for a long time: Having lived.

en-subjunctive.title: The subjunctive and formal style
en-subjunctive.theory.0.heading: Subjunctive after demands
en-subjunctive.theory.0.text: After **insist, demand, recommend, suggest, propose** and **it is essential / vital / important that**, formal English uses the base form without -s and without do: **that he be**, **that she leave**, **that it not be**. British English also allows **should + verb**.
en-subjunctive.theory.1.heading: The unreal past
en-subjunctive.theory.1.text: After **it’s (high) time, would rather, as if / as though, suppose** a past form talks about the present: It’s high time we **left**. I’d rather you **didn’t smoke**. He talks as if he **were** the boss.
en-subjunctive.theory.2.heading: Fixed expressions
en-subjunctive.exercises.4.explain: Would rather + another person + past: didn’t.
en-subjunctive.exercises.5.explain: The subjunctive negative is just not: that he not come.
en-subjunctive.exercises.6.explain: A fixed expression: Suffice it to say.
en-subjunctive.exercises.8.explain: After suggest that — the base form.
en-subjunctive.exercises.11.explain: A fixed expression: Come what may.

en-ellipsis.title: Ellipsis and substitution
en-ellipsis.summary: So do I, I hope so, I’d love to: how not to repeat what was said.
en-ellipsis.theory.0.heading: An auxiliary instead of the whole phrase
en-ellipsis.theory.0.text: Native speakers don’t repeat the whole verb: an auxiliary replaces it. **So + auxiliary + subject** means “me too”, **Neither / Nor** means “me neither”.
en-ellipsis.theory.1.heading: So / not instead of a clause
en-ellipsis.theory.1.text: After **think, hope, expect, suppose, be afraid**: I think **so**, I hope **not**, I’m afraid **not**, I don’t think **so**.
en-ellipsis.theory.2.heading: To without a verb, and one / ones
en-ellipsis.theory.2.text: **To** stands for a verb already mentioned: I’d love **to**. You don’t have **to**. A noun is replaced by **one / ones**: I don’t like the red shirt — I prefer the blue **one**.
en-ellipsis.exercises.0.explain: Repeat the auxiliary from the sentence: am.
en-ellipsis.exercises.1.explain: Neither + a positive auxiliary: neither did I.
en-ellipsis.exercises.5.explain: The auxiliary can stands for can fix it.
en-ellipsis.exercises.8.explain: Neither + a positive auxiliary: neither can I.
en-ellipsis.exercises.10.explain: To stands for borrow my car.

en-agreement.title: Agreement: is or are?
en-agreement.summary: The number of… is, a number of… are, neither… nor: tricky cases.
en-agreement.theory.0.heading: Tricky nouns
en-agreement.theory.0.text: **News, mathematics, physics, economics** are singular despite the -s: The news **is** good. **Police, people, cattle** are always plural: The police **are** here. **Team, family, government** can be either in British English, but singular is always safe.
en-agreement.theory.1.heading: Quantities
en-agreement.theory.1.text: **The number of** + noun is about the number itself, so the verb is singular: The number of students **is** growing. **A number of** = “several”, so plural: A number of students **are** absent. Sums, distances and periods count as one whole: Ten years **is** a long time. Fifty dollars **is** too much.
en-agreement.theory.2.heading: Pairs, each and one of
en-agreement.theory.2.text: With **neither … nor / either … or / not only … but also** the verb agrees with the **nearest** subject: Neither the teacher nor the students **were** ready. **Each, every, everybody, nobody** are singular. **One of the** + plural — the verb agrees with one: One of my friends **lives** in Rome. **None of** is formally singular, but both are common in speech.
en-agreement.exercises.2.explain: The number of is about the number: is.
en-agreement.exercises.4.explain: A distance as one whole: is.
en-agreement.exercises.5.explain: The nearest subject is parents: were.
en-agreement.exercises.6.explain: The nearest is the teacher: is.

es-ser-estar.title: Ser and estar: two verbs for “to be”
es-ser-estar.summary: Soy médico, estoy cansado: what is permanent, and what is a state or a place.
es-ser-estar.theory.0.text: **Ser** says what a person or thing is: name, job, origin, character, looks. **Estar** is about states and where things are.
es-ser-estar.theory.0.examples.0.translation: I’m a doctor. He’s from Mexico.
es-ser-estar.theory.0.examples.1.translation: I’m tired. Madrid is in Spain.
es-ser-estar.theory.1.heading: Conjugation
es-ser-estar.theory.1.text: Both verbs are irregular — the forms have to be learned.
es-ser-estar.theory.2.heading: The meaning changes
es-ser-estar.theory.2.text: With the same adjective, ser and estar give different meanings.
es-ser-estar.exercises.0.explain: What you do for a living — ser: soy estudiante.
es-ser-estar.exercises.4.explain: The soup has gone cold — a state, estar.
es-ser-estar.exercises.6.explain: “How are you?” is about a state: ¿Cómo estás?
es-ser-estar.exercises.7.translation: Madrid is in the centre of Spain.
es-ser-estar.exercises.10.explain: Days of the week and dates — ser.
es-ser-estar.exercises.11.translation: My father is a teacher, but he is on holiday now.

es-presente.title: Present tense: verbs in -ar, -er, -ir
es-presente.summary: Hablo, comes, vivimos: the endings of regular verbs.
es-presente.theory.0.text: Spanish verbs fall into three groups by their ending: **-ar, -er, -ir**. The ending is dropped and a personal ending is added to the stem.
es-presente.theory.1.heading: The pronoun can be left out
es-presente.theory.1.text: The ending already shows who is acting, so yo, tú, nosotros are usually not said. **Usted** (polite “you”) is conjugated like él.
es-presente.exercises.6.explain: Usted is conjugated like él: bebe.
es-presente.exercises.7.translation: We live in a small house.

es-genero.title: Noun gender and articles
es-genero.summary: El libro, la casa, unos amigos: gender, number and agreement.
es-genero.theory.0.text: Nouns in **-o** are usually masculine, nouns in **-a** feminine: el libro, la casa. Nouns in **-ción, -dad** are always feminine: la canción, la ciudad. There are exceptions: **el día, el mapa, el problema, la mano, la foto**.
es-genero.theory.1.heading: Adjectives agree
es-genero.theory.1.text: An adjective takes the gender and number of its noun and usually comes after it.
es-genero.theory.1.examples.0.translation: a red car — a red house
es-genero.exercises.3.explain: Ciudad in -dad is feminine, plural: las.
es-genero.exercises.5.explain: Día is an exception, masculine: un día.
es-genero.exercises.7.translation: The windows in the room are big.
es-genero.exercises.8.explain: Problema is masculine even though it ends in -a.
es-genero.exercises.9.explain: Mano is feminine even though it ends in -o.
es-genero.exercises.10.explain: Nouns in -dad are feminine: las ciudades.

es-gustar.title: The verb gustar: what I like
es-gustar.theory.0.text: Gustar works like “to please”: the thing you like is the subject, and who likes it is a pronoun **me, te, le, nos, os, les**. One thing or action — **gusta**, several things — **gustan**.
es-gustar.theory.1.heading: Who likes it
es-gustar.theory.1.text: For clarity or emphasis add **a + a name or pronoun**. In a negative, no goes before the pronoun.
es-gustar.exercises.10.explain: El chocolate is one thing: gusta.

es-indefinido.title: Pretérito indefinido: the finished past
es-indefinido.summary: Hablé, comiste, fuimos: what happened and is over.
es-indefinido.theory.0.text: The pretérito indefinido is for actions that happened and finished in the past. Signal words: **ayer, anoche, el año pasado, en 2019, hace dos días**.
es-indefinido.theory.1.heading: The accent changes the meaning
es-indefinido.theory.1.text: **hablo** — I speak, **habló** — he spoke. The accent mark is required here.
es-indefinido.theory.2.heading: Irregular verbs
es-indefinido.theory.2.text: Ser and ir share the same forms in this tense: **fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron**. Other common ones: tener → **tuve**, estar → **estuve**, hacer → **hice, hizo**.
es-indefinido.theory.2.examples.0.translation: Last summer we went to Peru.
es-indefinido.exercises.2.explain: Ir in the past, nosotros: fuimos.
es-indefinido.exercises.7.translation: Last night we watched a very good film.

es-gerundio.title: Estar + gerundio: what is happening now
es-gerundio.summary: Estoy leyendo — an action in progress.
es-gerundio.theory.0.text: To stress that an action is going on right now, use **estar + gerundio**. The gerund is formed like this: -ar → **-ando**, -er / -ir → **-iendo**.
es-gerundio.theory.1.heading: Special forms
es-gerundio.theory.1.text: If the stem ends in a vowel, -iendo becomes **-yendo**: leer → leyendo, oír → oyendo, ir → yendo. Some -ir verbs change the stem vowel: dormir → **durmiendo**, pedir → **pidiendo**, decir → **diciendo**.
es-gerundio.theory.1.examples.0.translation: I’m reading a very good book.
es-gerundio.exercises.2.explain: The stem ends in a vowel: leyendo.
es-gerundio.exercises.5.explain: A process takes only estar: estamos comiendo.

es-imperfecto.title: Imperfecto or indefinido
es-imperfecto.summary: Llovía, cuando llegué: background and event in the past.
es-imperfecto.theory.0.text: The **pretérito imperfecto** describes the background, past habits and “how things were”. Endings: -ar → **-aba**, -er / -ir → **-ía**. Only three verbs are irregular: **ser** (era), **ir** (iba), **ver** (veía).
es-imperfecto.theory.1.heading: Background and event
es-imperfecto.theory.1.text: Imperfecto — what was going on, the setting, a description (**llovía, era tarde, estaba cansado**). Indefinido — what happened, a finished action (**llegué, me llamó**). Imperfecto signal words: **antes, siempre, de niño, todos los días, mientras**.
es-imperfecto.theory.1.examples.0.translation: It was raining when I got home.
es-imperfecto.theory.1.examples.1.translation: As a child I lived in a village.
es-imperfecto.theory.1.examples.2.translation: Yesterday I saw Marta: she was very happy.
es-imperfecto.exercises.0.explain: The setting in childhood — imperfecto: vivía.
es-imperfecto.exercises.1.explain: The call is an event against the background: sonó.
es-imperfecto.exercises.3.explain: Time as background — imperfecto: eran las nueve.
es-imperfecto.exercises.4.explain: A finished action in a set period — indefinido.
es-imperfecto.exercises.6.explain: The call interrupted the sleep — indefinido.
es-imperfecto.exercises.7.translation: When I was a child, I read a lot.
es-imperfecto.exercises.11.translation: When I arrived, they were having dinner.

es-pronombres.title: Object pronouns: lo, la, le, se lo
es-pronombres.summary: Te lo doy, se lo digo: to whom and what.
es-pronombres.theory.0.text: The direct object (whom? what?) is **lo, la, los, las**. The indirect object (to whom?) is **le, les**. For me, you, us the forms are shared: **me, te, nos, os**. The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb.
es-pronombres.theory.1.heading: Two pronouns in a row
es-pronombres.theory.1.text: First “to whom”, then “what”: **me lo, te la**. When le / les meets lo / la, le turns into **se**: not “le lo” but **se lo**.
es-pronombres.theory.1.examples.1.translation: Are you giving Ana the present? — Yes, I am.
es-pronombres.theory.2.heading: With infinitives, gerunds and commands
es-pronombres.theory.2.text: Pronouns can be attached to the end: **voy a comprarlo**, **estoy leyéndolo**, and in a positive command they must be: **¡Dímelo!** (the stress keeps its accent mark).
es-pronombres.exercises.5.explain: A positive command: Dime (one pronoun — no accent mark).
es-pronombres.exercises.7.translation: I’ll explain it to you tomorrow.
es-pronombres.exercises.11.explain: Command + me + lo, the stress keeps its mark: dámelo.

es-subjuntivo.title: Presente de subjuntivo: wishes and requests
es-subjuntivo.summary: Quiero que vengas: when you want someone else to act.
es-subjuntivo.theory.0.text: The subjunctive is needed when one person wants, asks or advises **someone else** to do something: **querer que, esperar que, pedir que, es importante que**. With the same subject — just the infinitive: Quiero **venir**, but Quiero que **vengas**.
es-subjuntivo.theory.0.examples.0.translation: I want you to come to my party.
es-subjuntivo.theory.1.heading: How to form it
es-subjuntivo.theory.1.text: Take the yo form of the present, drop the -o and add the “opposite” endings: -ar verbs get **-e**, -er / -ir verbs get **-a**. Tener → teng-o → **tenga**, hacer → **haga**, venir → **venga**. Own forms: **ser (sea), ir (vaya), estar (esté), saber (sepa), haber (haya), dar (dé)**.
es-subjuntivo.theory.2.heading: Wishes
es-subjuntivo.theory.2.text: After **ojalá** and in wishes with **que**: ¡Ojalá **haga** sol! ¡Que **tengas** buen viaje!
es-subjuntivo.exercises.7.translation: I hope you like the present.
es-subjuntivo.exercises.11.explain: I hope and I see — one subject, so the infinitive.

es-por-para.title: Por and para
es-por-para.summary: For whom, what for, through what and why.
es-por-para.theory.0.heading: Para — purpose and direction
es-por-para.theory.0.text: **Para** looks ahead: purpose (**para aprender**), recipient (**para ti**), destination (**salgo para Madrid**), deadline (**para el lunes**), opinion (**para mí**).
es-por-para.theory.0.examples.1.translation: I study to find a good job.
es-por-para.theory.1.heading: Por — cause and route
es-por-para.theory.1.text: **Por** explains “because of what” and “through what”: cause (**por la lluvia**), movement through a place (**paseamos por el parque**), time of day (**por la mañana**), means (**por teléfono**), exchange and price (**lo compré por 10 euros**), “instead of” (**trabajo por ti**), the doer in the passive (**escrito por Cervantes**).
es-por-para.theory.1.examples.1.translation: We didn’t go out because of the cold.
es-por-para.exercises.11.explain: The doer in the passive — por.

es-si-imperfecto.title: Si tuviera…: unreal conditions
es-si-imperfecto.theory.0.text: An imagined condition in the present: **si + imperfecto de subjuntivo, condicional**. Like English If I had…, I would…
es-si-imperfecto.theory.0.examples.0.translation: If I had money, I would travel the world.
es-si-imperfecto.theory.0.examples.1.translation: If I were you, I wouldn’t do that.
es-si-imperfecto.theory.1.text: Take the ellos form of the indefinido, drop -ron and add **-ra**: tuvieron → **tuviera**, fueron → **fuera**, hablaron → **hablara**, pudieron → **pudiera**. The nosotros form has an accent: **tuviéramos**.
es-si-imperfecto.theory.2.text: Infinitive + **-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían**: viajaría, comería. Irregular stems as in the future: **tendr-, har-, podr-, dir-, saldr-, vendr-, querr-, sabr-**.
es-si-imperfecto.theory.2.examples.0.translation: If I could, I would tell you.
es-si-imperfecto.exercises.7.translation: If I knew Spanish, I would live in Madrid.

es-cuando.title: Cuando + subjuntivo: the future in a time clause
es-cuando.summary: Cuando llegues, llámame: a time that hasn’t come yet.
es-cuando.theory.0.text: After **cuando, en cuanto, hasta que, tan pronto como, antes de que, después de que**, the future is expressed with the **subjunctive**, not the future tense.
es-cuando.theory.1.heading: Habits and the past
es-cuando.theory.1.text: For what usually happens or already happened — the indicative: Cuando **llego** a casa, ceno (always). Cuando **llegué**, cené (yesterday).
es-cuando.theory.2.heading: Antes de que — always subjunctive
es-cuando.theory.2.text: **Antes de que** takes the subjunctive in any tense, and with the same subject becomes **antes de + infinitive**: Salgo antes de que **llueva**. Me lavo las manos antes de **comer**.
es-cuando.exercises.7.translation: When you finish, write to me.

es-pluscuamperfecto.title: Si hubiera sabido…: the unreal past
es-pluscuamperfecto.summary: Pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo and condicional compuesto.
es-pluscuamperfecto.theory.0.text: Regret about a past that can no longer be changed: **si + hubiera + participio, habría + participio**.
es-pluscuamperfecto.theory.0.examples.0.translation: If I had known, I would have come.
es-pluscuamperfecto.theory.0.examples.1.translation: If you had studied, you would have passed.
es-pluscuamperfecto.theory.1.heading: Mixed conditionals
es-pluscuamperfecto.theory.1.text: A past condition with a result now: **si + hubiera + participio, condicional simple**. Si **hubiera aceptado** aquel trabajo, ahora **viviría** en Londres.
es-pluscuamperfecto.theory.2.heading: Other uses
es-pluscuamperfecto.theory.2.text: After **ojalá** — regret about the past: ¡Ojalá **hubiera ido**! After past verbs with que: Me alegré de que **hubieras venido**. In speech, **hubiera** often replaces habría: Si lo hubiera sabido, **hubiera venido**.
es-pluscuamperfecto.exercises.2.explain: Mixed: the result is now — sería.
es-pluscuamperfecto.exercises.3.explain: Regret about the past: hubiera dicho.
es-pluscuamperfecto.exercises.4.explain: A condition in the past: hubiéramos traído.
es-pluscuamperfecto.exercises.6.explain: After que in the past — hubieras avisado.
es-pluscuamperfecto.exercises.7.translation: If I had known, I would have told you.
es-pluscuamperfecto.exercises.10.explain: Regret about the past: hubieras venido.
es-pluscuamperfecto.exercises.11.translation: If you had called me, I would have helped you.

es-estilo-indirecto.title: Estilo indirecto: reported speech
es-estilo-indirecto.summary: Dijo que estaba cansada: how to pass on someone’s words.
es-estilo-indirecto.theory.0.text: After **dijo que, comentó que, explicó que** the tense moves back when you report the words later.
es-estilo-indirecto.theory.1.heading: Requests and questions
es-estilo-indirecto.theory.1.text: An order or a request turns into the **imperfecto de subjuntivo**: Me pidió que **cerrara** la puerta. A yes / no question is introduced with **si**, others with a question word that keeps its accent: Me preguntó **si** tenía hambre; Me preguntó **dónde** vivía.
es-estilo-indirecto.theory.2.heading: Time and place words
es-estilo-indirecto.theory.2.text: hoy → **aquel día**, mañana → **al día siguiente**, ayer → **el día anterior**, aquí → **allí**, este → **aquel**. Venir often becomes **ir**, traer becomes **llevar**.
es-estilo-indirecto.exercises.3.explain: An order in the past — imperfecto de subjuntivo.
es-estilo-indirecto.exercises.7.translation: She said she would come the next day.

es-se.title: Se: impersonal and passive sentences
es-se.theory.0.text: When “people in general” act, with no specific person: **se + verb in the 3rd person singular.** Se vive bien aquí. ¿Cómo **se dice** esto en español?
es-se.theory.1.text: If there is an object, the verb agrees with it: **se vende** piso, **se venden** pisos. This is far more common than the passive with ser.
es-se.theory.2.heading: Se for accidents
es-se.theory.2.text: **se + me / te / le + verb**: the action happened “by itself”, without intent. The verb agrees with the thing: **Se me olvidó** la llave; **se me olvidaron** las llaves; **se le rompió** el vaso.
es-se.exercises.3.explain: It agrees with las llaves: olvidaron.
es-se.exercises.4.explain: Who it happened to — le: se le rompió.
es-se.exercises.9.explain: It agrees with el móvil: rompió.

es-concesivas.title: Concessive clauses: aunque
es-concesivas.summary: Aunque llueve or aunque llueva — one letter makes the difference.
es-concesivas.theory.0.text: After **aunque** the choice of mood changes the meaning. The **indicative** is a fact the speaker accepts: Aunque **llueve**, salimos (it is raining, but we’re going out). The **subjunctive** is a possibility or a fact that doesn’t matter to the speaker: Aunque **llueva**, saldremos (even if it rains).
es-concesivas.theory.0.examples.0.translation: Although it’s expensive, I’m buying it.
es-concesivas.theory.0.examples.1.translation: Even if it’s expensive, I’ll buy it.
es-concesivas.theory.0.examples.2.translation: Even if I were a millionaire, I wouldn’t do that.
es-concesivas.theory.1.heading: Other concessive links
es-concesivas.theory.1.text: **A pesar de que** and **por más que** behave like aunque. **Por mucho que / por muy + adjective + que** almost always take the subjunctive: Por mucho que **insistas**, no voy. Por muy listo que **sea**… Literary **si bien** takes only the indicative. Repeated verb: **Digas lo que digas**, no cambiaré de opinión.
es-concesivas.exercises.0.explain: A fact in the past — indicative.
es-concesivas.exercises.3.explain: A repeated-verb pattern, both verbs in the subjunctive: Digan lo que digan.
es-concesivas.exercises.7.translation: Even if it rains, we’ll go for a walk.
es-concesivas.exercises.8.explain: An accepted fact in the past — indicative.
es-concesivas.exercises.11.translation: Although I’m tired, I’ll finish the work.

es-perifrasis.title: Verbal periphrases
es-perifrasis.theory.0.text: Periphrases combine an auxiliary verb with an infinitive, a gerund or a participle. They express shades of meaning that English often conveys with adverbs.
es-perifrasis.theory.1.heading: Llevar and seguir
es-perifrasis.theory.1.text: **Llevar** + time + gerundio = “I have been doing it for…”: **Llevo** tres horas **esperando**. The negative is **sin + infinitive**: Llevo dos días **sin dormir**. **Seguir** never takes an infinitive: not “sigue a llover” but **sigue lloviendo**.
es-perifrasis.exercises.7.translation: I’ve been waiting for you for an hour.
es-perifrasis.exercises.11.explain: tener + participio agrees with the object: escritos.

es-probabilidad.title: Future and conditional of probability
es-probabilidad.summary: ¿Qué hora será? — Serán las diez: how to say “probably”.
es-probabilidad.theory.0.text: In Spanish the future tense often talks not about the future but about a **guess**. Instead of “probably” or “must be”, the verb simply moves one step forward.
es-probabilidad.theory.0.table.rows.3.2: He had probably already left (by then).
es-probabilidad.theory.1.heading: Choosing the tense
es-probabilidad.theory.1.text: About the present — **futuro simple** (estará, tendrá). About the recent past that would be pretérito perfecto — **futuro compuesto** (habrá llegado). About the past — **condicional** (estaría, sería). About something before another past event — **condicional compuesto** (habría perdido).
es-probabilidad.theory.1.examples.0.translation: Juan isn’t answering. He must be asleep.
es-probabilidad.theory.1.examples.1.translation: He didn’t come yesterday. He must have been ill.
es-probabilidad.theory.2.heading: Concession
es-probabilidad.theory.2.text: The future also means “it may be…, but”: **Será** caro, pero merece la pena. — It may be expensive, but it’s worth it.
es-probabilidad.exercises.1.explain: A guess about the present — future.
es-probabilidad.exercises.2.explain: A guess about the past — condicional.
es-probabilidad.exercises.3.explain: The recent past — futuro compuesto: habré dejado.
es-probabilidad.exercises.4.explain: A guess about something that just happened: habrá ido.
es-probabilidad.exercises.5.explain: A guess about the past — serían.
es-probabilidad.exercises.8.explain: Before another past event — condicional compuesto.
es-probabilidad.exercises.9.explain: Habrá llovido — it must have rained.
es-probabilidad.exercises.10.explain: A guess about something recent: ¿Qué habrá pasado?
